column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Every joint of a person owes a charity every day on which the sun rises. Judging justly between two people is a charity;

helping a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or lifting his belongings onto it, is a charity; a good word is a charity; every step you take towards the prayer is a charity; and removing something harmful from the road is a charity.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
Sulāmā (“joint”): the joints of a person, which according to a hadith number 360.
The printed text reads 36; the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim gives the number of joints as 360.
“Judging justly between two people”: reconciling and judging between two disputants.
“Helping a man”: assisting him to mount his animal or lifting his belongings onto it for him.
“A good word”: the opposite of an evil word.
“Removing something harmful”: putting aside whatever harms passers-by: filth, thorns, stones and the like.
Khaṭwah, with fatḥah: a single stepping; with ḍammah, the distance between the two feet.
The arrangement of the human being's bones and joints is among the greatest blessings of Allah upon the servant, so he needs to give charity for them.
It is recommended to persevere in voluntary deeds every day.
Charity is not confined to wealth; it is also in deeds and other things.
The virtue of reconciling between people and judging between them with justice.
Urging attendance at the congregational prayers and walking to them for the prayer.
Encouragement to remove harmful things from the road.
Encouragement to lofty manners and high character.
The noble Prophet ﷺ tells us in this hadith that every limb of a person owes a charity every day,

thanking and praising Allah for having composed these limbs in him and fashioned them well, outwardly and inwardly; had He willed, He would have taken away their ability, and the person could not move or carry out his religious or worldly tasks.

Their being kept for him, their continuance and the continuance of their strength require gratitude from the servant by giving charity because of the continuance of this blessing; and every good deed—such as reconciling between people,

judging between them with justice, spreading the greeting of peace, speaking kindly, helping those who need help, and giving sincere advice to the Muslims in word and deed—each one of these contains a charity. On this meaning the poet said:
Never lose interest in doing kindness to anyone; / the man who is denied kindness is truly deprived.
Good remains, however long it is hidden, / and evil, as long as a man lives, is blamed.
Another poet:
If you do not sow, and then see a harvester, / you will regret your neglect in the season of sowing.
